question: A radioactive nucleus emits an alpha particle. Explain how the mass number and atomic number of the daughter nucleus change, and why energy may be released in the process.

options.A: On $\alpha$ emission, mass number decreases by $2$ and atomic number decreases by $4$; energy is released because charge is destroyed.
options.B: On $\alpha$ emission, mass number and atomic number remain unchanged; energy is released only from electron transitions.
options.C: On $\alpha$ emission, mass number decreases by $4$ and atomic number increases by $2$; energy is released because nuclear radius increases.
options.D:
An $\alpha$ particle contains $2$ protons and $2$ neutrons. Thus the daughter has mass number $A-4$ and atomic number $Z-2$.
If the parent mass exceeds the total product mass, the difference $\Delta m$ is released as energy, $E=\Delta mc^2$.
